solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pay for train fare here?

parts.note: surface reading: the ticket office where you buy your rail ticket
setter's reading: fare as food eaten on a train, so the place is the carriage selling snacks

explanation.surface: A passenger asks where to buy a ticket for the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Fare means the cost of a ticket, but it also means food; the carriage where you pay for food on a train is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is the railway carriage where travellers purchase meals and drinks during the journey.

clue.text: Club European duke held?

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Asks whether a continental nobleman was detained by a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held' is not about a duke being held; it is the definition, as in waiting with bated breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Bated means restrained or held back, surviving mainly in the idiom 'with bated breath'.

clue.text: Folly as Pope forced to feed cook

indicators.note: feeding puts something inside, so these letters go into the next word
something forced is pushed out of its natural shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of Pope rearranged
to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A pontiff is foolishly made to feed the kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pontiff sits between the first letter and the rest of the cooking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Foppery is foolish vanity or a silly affectation, so it serves as a synonym for folly.

clue.text: Transport going round British plant

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: transport here is a state of rapture or delight
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Some vehicle travelling around a British plant or factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport means rapture, not vehicles: 'transports of delight'. The B sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is the spurge genus of flowering plants, including the poinsettia.

clue.text: Happily under canvas in cold and alone?

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on a tap

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the canvas word goes within the others

parts.note: alone in the sense of solely
living under canvas means camping in a tent

explanation.surface: Someone camping alone in the cold is contented, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The tent word splits the word for alone after its first two letters, and C leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentedly means in a satisfied, pleased way, which matches the adverb happily.

clue.text: Over years artist makes Scandinavian rug

indicators.note: something over something else covers it, so the artist wraps around the years

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An artist has woven a Nordic rug over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts, goes around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A rya is a thick-piled knotted rug traditional in Sweden and Finland.

clue.text: Antelope, any number in valley returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the valley word is read backwards
one thing in another sits inside it, so the number goes within the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
n is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: Antelopes of any number are coming back into a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiralled horns.

clue.text: Wear armour regularly — mistake

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Advice that wearing armour all the time is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake; the two words are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Jar with no lid for insect repellent, first-class?

indicators.note: a lid is the top, so with no lid the first letter is taken off

parts.note: camphor is used to keep moths away
A is a first-class grade, as in A1

explanation.surface: A jar of insect repellent missing its lid: is that first-class?
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is an ancient two-handled jar used for wine or oil.

clue.text: Which doctor off ers in sea dogs to be cured

indicators.note: curing changes a condition, so the letters are treated and reshaped

parts.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor's offer to cure sick old sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The source splits 'offers' as 'off ers'. Sea dogs are old sailors, but the words are only letters here; 'Which doctor' hints at witch doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor identifies an illness, so what a doctor offers is a verdict on the illness, used as a verb.

clue.text: Notice back leg that generates Swiatek's advantage?

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the notice word is read from its end

parts.note: to spot is to notice
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: A tennis star's strong back leg gives her an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Iga Swiatek is a Polish tennis champion known for heavy spin on her forehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin is forward rotation on a tennis ball, a weapon that helps a player win points.

clue.text: Roman general an old man without control

indicators.note: without here means outside, so these letters go around the next idea

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a grip on something is control of it
pa is father

explanation.surface: An old Roman general who has lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in older English it means outside, so the old man and the article wrap the word for control.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's leading general, victor at Actium.

clue.text: Maradona's pass away before game?

parts.note: to die is to pass away
go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Did the footballer Maradona die before a match?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' tempts a football reading, but pass away means die.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona was the Argentine footballer, so his first name is the answer.

clue.text: Did you say Neo had a blue bedcover?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: Neo is the setter, so I; had is 'd; blue means down, as in sad

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the setter owned a blue quilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their own pen-name, so Neo is I. Blue is the mood, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with soft feathers, originally from the eider duck.

clue.text: Snake in sports field, far end

parts.note: a baseball field is a diamond
the back is the far end

explanation.surface: A snake is lurking at the far end of a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamondback is a rattlesnake named for the diamond pattern on its scales.

clue.text: Horse to howl as dog

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to bark long and deep like a hound

explanation.surface: A horse made to howl like a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay names a brown horse with black points, and is also the verb for a hound's deep cry.

clue.text: Bewildered wabbit hunter left to fill sack

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so these letters sit within the sack word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
Elmer Fudd, as initial and surname, hunts Bugs Bunny, calling him a 'wabbit'
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A confused rabbit hunter left to fill a sack with game.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmer Fudd, the Looney Tunes hunter, can't say his Rs, hence 'wabbit'; he is shortened to his initial and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Befuddled means muddled or confused, a synonym of bewildered.

clue.text: 17 among these Scotsmen with motorists in city

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the motorists go within the city

parts.note: Bath, the spa city in Somerset
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: Scotsmen join motorists in a city, among them the answer to 17.
explanation.walkthrough: The 17 answer names frogs and toads; the definition is a group they belong to.
explanation.definitionFit: Batrachians are the tailless amphibians, the order that includes both frogs and toads.

clue.text: Sybarites from Wear in robberies

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the wear word goes into the robberies

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
to don is to put on or wear

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers come from the River Wear after robberies.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W suggests the river in north-east England; it is just the verb to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybarites are lovers of luxury and pleasure, the same as hedonists.

clue.text: Good rant AfD spoiled in a way?

indicators.note: something spoiled is wrecked out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A political rant from Germany's far-right AfD party gets spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Cockney rhyming slang, where frog and toad means road.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang frog and toad stands for road, and a road is a way.

clue.text: Enigmatic alumnus safe outside clubs

parts.note: an old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the safe word wraps around the clubs

parts.note: safe in the sense of certain or secure
the card suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A mysterious former student keeps a safe outside the clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is unclear or hard to understand, as an enigmatic thing is.

clue.text: Recognised driver in Chelsea?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the next word, among its letters

parts.note: letters two to four

explanation.surface: A famous motorist spotted in the London district of Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Driver is not a motorist: Ernie Els is the South African golfer, and a driver is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Els is a renowned golfer celebrated for powerful, easy tee shots with his driver.

clue.text: Accolades? I'm no ace, unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone modestly declines praise, saying they are no ace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is self-deprecation, the opposite of what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia, plural of encomium, are formal expressions of high praise or tributes.

clue.text: Ruined small city once involved in action

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it, so these go within the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
standard abbreviation
Troy is an ancient city

explanation.surface: A small ancient city was ruined in some action long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroyed means wrecked beyond repair, so it matches ruined as a past participle.

clue.text: Beams reflected back and forth?

parts.note: surface reading: light or radio waves bouncing to and fro
setter's reading: the word itself is the same read backwards or forwards

explanation.walkthrough: The system sends out beams that are reflected back, and its name is a palindrome, reading the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar detects objects by sending out radio waves and catching the echoes reflected from them.

clue.text: Iridescent material from northern land area

parts.note: standard abbreviation
an acre is a measure of land area

explanation.surface: A shimmering substance found in a region of the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the shimmering lining of some shells.

clue.text: Foden crocked? That's that!

indicators.note: crocked means injured or broken, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Foden lorry, or player Phil Foden, is crocked, and that's the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Foden is a British lorry maker and an England footballer; 'end of' is British slang closing an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'end of' is colloquial for 'end of discussion', declaring the matter closed.

clue.text: Wash flooded Californian city?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a flooded place is under water

explanation.surface: Would a flood wash out a Californian city?
explanation.walkthrough: The city comes second in the clue but first in the answer, with 'flooded' read as under.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them, as in a laundry.

clue.text: Tear open late message: almost ready?

parts.note: first meaning: to tear apart
second meaning: the initials on a gravestone for the dead

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Someone rips open a late message to see if the matter is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: two definitions and a third route through wordplay. The late are the dead, and RIP stands for rest in peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip is to tear, and RIP, rest in peace, is the message carved for the deceased.

clue.text: Adopted as 500 birds flown back?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: flying back means returning the way it came, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
emus are flightless birds

explanation.surface: Were five hundred birds adopted when they flew home?
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that emus cannot fly at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means taken on, as one adopts a name or a manner.

clue.text: Dull and tedious day with parent

parts.note: standard abbreviation
to parent a child is to rear it

explanation.surface: A boring, tedious day spent with a parent.
explanation.walkthrough: Parent looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a literary form of dreary, meaning gloomy and dull.

clue.text: Fish second Welsh river — not with this rod!

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
standard abbreviation
the Taff flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: An angler is warned off using a certain rod for fish on a Welsh river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not with this' is a joke: a pikestaff is a pole, not a fishing rod, despite the pike inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikestaff is a wooden staff or walking pole with a metal point, a kind of rod.
